We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction (one step) for target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Let's decode: It's an alkene attached to phenyl and a cyclopentanol with CF3 group? Actually structure: a terminal alkene (CH2= C(aryl) - chiral carbon attached to cyclopentane bearing OH and CF3). So target is product of carbonyl-ene reaction: forward reaction: carbonyl-ene: carbonyl + alkene -> allylic alcohol. In retrosynthesis, we break the C-O bond to get a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene (with allylic hydrogen). So precursor would be a ketone (maybe a cyclopentanone with CF3) and an alkene (maybe a phenyl-substituted alkene). The carbonyl-ene forms a new C-C bond between carbonyl carbon and alkene carbon, and creates an OH at the allylic position.

Thus retrosynthetic step: target -> precursors: (1) a ketone: maybe C1: cyclopentanone with CF3 at carbonyl carbon? Actually product has OH at carbon 13 (the carbon bearing OH). In carbonyl-ene, the OH ends up at the allylic carbon (the carbon that originally had the allylic hydrogen). So the carbon bearing OH in product corresponds to the carbonyl carbon? Wait typical carbonyl-ene: carbonyl (C=O) + alkene (C=C-H) -> new C-C bond between carbonyl carbon and alkene carbon, and OH ends up on the carbonyl oxygen? Actually product is an allylic alcohol where the OH is on the carbon that was the carbonyl carbon? Let's recall: carbonyl-ene (also called Alder-ene) yields an allylic alcohol where the carbonyl oxygen becomes OH attached to the carbonyl carbon which becomes a new C-C bond. So the carbonyl carbon becomes a tertiary carbon bearing OH. So in product, the carbon bearing OH is the former carbonyl carbon. So precursor: a ketone (maybe cyclopentanone with CF3) and an alkene (phenyl-substituted alkene). The new bond formed is between carbonyl carbon (C=O) and the alkene carbon (the one bearing the allylic hydrogen). In product, the carbon bearing OH is attached to the alkene carbon (now sp3). So we need to identify the precursor structures.

Target: CH2= C(aryl) - chiral carbon attached to cyclopentane ring (C1-4) with OH at carbon 13 (the carbon attached to CF3). So the carbon bearing OH is attached to the alkene carbon (C2). So precursor: a ketone where that carbon is carbonyl carbon attached to cyclopentane and CF3, and the alkene is CH2= C(aryl)-H (i.e., an alkene with an allylic hydrogen at the carbon that will become attached). The alkene must have an allylic hydrogen on the carbon that will bond to carbonyl carbon. In product, the carbon attached to OH (C13) is attached to C2 (the alkene carbon). So the alkene precursor likely is CH2= C(H)-Ar (i.e., styrene). The allylic hydrogen is on the internal carbon (C2) which is attached to phenyl and CH2. So the alkene is styrene (C=CH2 attached to phenyl). Actually styrene is Ph-CH=CH2. The internal carbon (CH) has H (allylic) and phenyl. That matches.

Thus precursor 1: styrene (C=CH2 attached to phenyl). Precursor 2: cyclopentanone with CF3 at carbonyl carbon? Wait carbonyl carbon is attached to cyclopentane ring (the carbonyl carbon is part of the ring? In product, the carbon bearing OH is part of the cyclopentane ring (C13). The cyclopentane ring is attached to that carbon (C13) as part of the ring. So the carbonyl carbon in precursor is part of the cyclopentane ring (i.e., a cyclopentanone). The carbonyl carbon is part of the ring, bearing CF3 substituent. So precursor: 3,3,3-trifluorocyclopentanone (i.e., cyclopentanone with CF3 at carbonyl carbon). Actually carbonyl carbon is part of ring; CF3 attached to carbonyl carbon? In product, CF3 attached to carbon bearing OH (C13). So in precursor, CF3 attached to carbonyl carbon (C=O). So the precursor is 3,3,3-trifluorocyclopentanone (or maybe 2,2,2-trifluoro-? need to check). The carbonyl carbon is part of ring, with CF3 substituent.

Thus retrosynthetic step: target -> styrene + 3,3,3-trifluorocyclopentanone.

Now we need to find a template that matches this transformation. The earlier search gave template 1209837 which seems to be a carbonyl-ene? The retro_smarts_template: '[C:3]-[C:2](-[C:4])-[OH;D1;+0:1]>>C-C(=C)-C(=O)-[O;H0;D2;+0:1]-[C:2](-[C:3])-[C:4]'. This is a retro transformation: product (alkyl-CH(OH)-C) to carbonyl + alkene. So applying this template to target should give precursors: an alkene and a carbonyl. Let's try applying template 1209837 to target. Use apply_template with that template id. Already attempted apply_template with molecule_smiles "C=C(c1ccccc1)C1CCCC1C(=O)C(F)(F)F" and template 1209837 gave empty result. Maybe need correct SMILES for target (including stereochemistry). Our target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Simplify to canonical: C=C(c1ccccc1)C1CCCC1C(=O)C(F)(F)F? Wait product has OH not carbonyl. The target has OH at C13, not carbonyl. So the SMILES we used earlier (C=C(c1ccccc1)C1CCCC1C(=O)C(F)(F)F) is the precursor (ketone). The target is with OH. So we need to apply template to target (with OH) to get ketone + alkene. Let's construct target SMILES without atom mapping: maybe "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CCCC1C(O)C(F)(F)F". That's the product. Let's try apply_template with that SMILES.
